name: sashamarchuk-plugins
description: Sasha Marchuk's Claude Code plugins — opinionated tooling for ticket management, automation, and everyday engineering workflows.

plugins.name: clickup
plugins.description: Universal /clickup skill for creating and managing ClickUp tickets with enforced quality standards — Connextra user stories, evidence-only descriptions, fuzzy list aliases, first-name teammate resolution, duplicate detection, idempotent create, and a two-step onboarding wizard. Works over any ClickUp transport (ClickUp MCP, the clickup-cli binary, or the raw REST API) through one configurable connection layer — on first use it investigates what's available, asks which transport to use, and remembers the choice (/clickup:connect); nothing about the transport is hardcoded.

plugins.name: ultra
plugins.description: Provides /ultra:run (and /ultra:resume) — multi-agent swarm with adversarial validation, structured debates, devil's advocate, and anti-AI-slop checks. Always invoked as /ultra:run (never bare /ultra). Supports tiers (--small/--medium/--large/--xl), multi-terminal coordination, and wrapping other skills.

plugins.name: ultra-analyzer
plugins.description: (beta) Rigorous pipeline analyzer. Discover → Analyze → Validate → Synthesize, with resume-able state and /ultra:run validation gates at critical boundaries. Source-agnostic: MongoDB, filesystem, PDF corpora, web scrapes, logs, JSON/CSV. Requires the `ultra` plugin from this same marketplace.

plugins.name: g-event
plugins.description: Universal /g-event skill for scheduling, updating, and cancelling Google Calendar events with Google Meet — always attaches a configurable notes bot, conflict detection, past-time guard, two-step onboarding (identity + calendar defaults). Reads teammates from ~/.claude/shared/identity.json, the same file the `clickup` plugin uses, so names resolve the same way in both.

plugins.name: claude-migrate
plugins.description: (beta) Universal Claude-to-Claude account migrator. Parse a Claude.ai data export (or extract live from the old account) -> deterministically score each chat's value -> you confirm what migrates -> distill every kept chat into one paste-ready first message -> re-create projects and seed chats in the new account. Always builds a byte-exact, self-contained copy page (zero tooling, the reliable floor); when a pre-authenticated browser is reachable it also runs confirmation-gated automation (seed -> await OK -> rename, then strips the onboarding instruction). Resume-able state machine with /ultra gates. Requires the `ultra` plugin from this same marketplace.

plugins.name: find-call
plugins.description: (beta) Universal /find-call skill — pull deep, cited context from your past Google Calendar meetings. Searches Calendar + optional transcripts (Sembly or any connected notetaker) in parallel, reads the notes-bot "Meeting Resources" block (Transcription, Meeting Notes, Video, Parent Folder), disambiguates matches, and spawns sonnet sub-agents per call for transcript-depth. Uses whatever calendar/doc/transcript tools are available by default — set a preferred provider per source via `/find-call:config` (always with fallback, so the data is retrieved by any working method) and inspect resolution via `/find-call:status`. Resolves teammate names against ~/.claude/shared/identity.json, the same roster `clickup` and `g-event` use. Investigation is read-only — never modifies Calendar, Drive, or transcripts.

plugins.name: log-time
plugins.description: (beta) Universal /log-time skill — reconstruct what you actually worked on and produce a paste-ready time-log for Redmine (or any tracker your config describes) by cross-checking the evidence sources you configure: calendar, task tracker, Claude Code session history, meeting transcripts, spreadsheets, or any custom source you can describe in plain text. Behavior is driven by a free-form markdown config (~/.claude/log-time/config.md) written by a four-step, fully skippable onboarding wizard (/log-time:onboard) and editable any time via /log-time:config; a first run with no config routes straight into onboarding. Evidence-only by default: no fabricated hours and no assumed daily target. Pairs well with the find-call plugin for transcript-depth call context. Read-only against every source — writes only its own config and per-run artifacts.

plugins.name: harness
plugins.description: (beta) Universal autonomous orchestration harness — runs Claude Code sessions in real terminals to execute your ticket queue end-to-end (GSD-flavored by default), unattended. Deterministic bash engine: user + project config, model fallback chains with '|' OR syntax (fable|mythos|opus), GitHub-issues or local-file tickets with a mandatory readiness grill gate, rate-limit PAUSE (never stop) with API-timed auto-resume, tty-keyed session registry, and a graceful /exit-then-close terminal lifecycle. One account by default; any account switcher pluggable via one config key.

plugins.name: task-launch
plugins.description: Open ONE fresh coding session for ONE in-progress task (default: Claude Code in a new iTerm2 tab — launcher and coding tool configurable), in the right folder, seeded with the task's context + related call transcripts (loaded fresh via the configured transcript loader) + any verbatim pass-through material + a rule to report back to the tracker when done. /task-launch:run --all launches every in-progress task in one pass — parallel per-task analysis, ONE consolidated confirmation, still one terminal per task — and the default launch mode (all vs one) is configurable. Runs standalone or right after morning-brief; tracker-agnostic and config-driven via ~/.claude/task-launch/config.json (set up with /task-launch:onboard, inspect with /task-launch:status). One task = one session; always a fresh session; the launcher only opens sessions — the report-back is a rule each child session follows — and never runs or monitors them (that's the harness).

plugins.name: ig-dm-export-analyzer
plugins.description: (beta) Turn an Instagram "Download Your Information" export into a clean, analysable chat corpus — one JSON file per conversation plus a filterable index.json rollup. Repairs Meta's UTF-8-as-Latin-1 mojibake, merges message_N.json pagination, filters strictly by date range and excluded threads, resolves media across split text/media archives, and transcribes voice notes and video audio tracks through a configurable speech-to-text provider (Soniox cloud, local whisper.cpp, or none). Every machine transcription is labeled four independent ways so it can never be mistaken for something the person typed, and a self-consistency verifier reconciles the output against the raw export. Fully config-driven: a new export is a new config file, not a code change.
